ρααβ.def: of Hebrew origin ((G7343)); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess. KJV: Rahab.

ραββι.def: of Hebrew origin (H7227 with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor. KJV: Master, Rabbi.

ραββονι.def: of Chaldee origin; corresponding to ῥαββί (G4461). KJV: Lord, Rabboni.

ραβδιζω.def: from ῥάβδος (G4464); to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado. KJV: beat (with rods).

ραβδοσ.def: from the base of ῥαπίζω (G4474); a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty). KJV: rod, sceptre, staff.

ραβδουχοσ.def: from ῥάβδος (G4464) and ἔχω (G2192); a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner). KJV: serjeant.

ραγαυ.def: of Hebrew origin (H7466); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch. KJV: Ragau.

ραδιουργημα.def: from a comparative of ῥᾴδιος (easy, i.e. reckless) and ἔργον (G2041); easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime. KJV: lewdness.

ραδιουργια.def: from the same as ῥᾳδιούργημα (G4467); recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity. KJV: mischief.

ρακα.def: of Chaldee origin (compare H7386); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification). KJV: Raca.

ρακοσ.def: from ῥήγνυμι (G4486); a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth. KJV: cloth.

ραμα.def: of Hebrew origin (H7414); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine. KJV: Rama.

ραντιζω.def: from a derivative of ῥαίνω (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively). KJV: sprinkle.

ραντισμοσ.def: from ῥαντίζω (G4472); aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively). KJV: sprinkling.

ραπιζω.def: from a derivative of a primary ῥέπω (to let fall, "rap"); to slap. KJV: smite (with the palm of the hand).

ραπισμα.def: from ῥαπίζω (G4474); a slap. KJV: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.

ραφισ.def: from a primary ῥάπτω (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω (G4474) through the idea of puncturing); a needle. KJV: needle.

ραχαβ.def: from the same as Ῥαάβ (G4460); Rachab, a Canaanitess. KJV: Rachab.

ραχηλ.def: of Hebrew origin (H7354); Rachel, the wife of Jacob. KJV: Rachel.

ρεβεκκα.def: of Hebrew origin (H7259); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac. KJV: Rebecca.

ρεδα.def: of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding). KJV: chariot.

ρεμφαν.def: by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (H3594); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol. KJV: Remphan.

ρεω.def: a primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form ῥεύω is used to flow ("run"; as water). KJV: flow.
perhaps akin (or identical) with ῥέω (G4482) (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. speak or say. KJV: command, make, say, speak (of).

ρηγιον.def: of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy. KJV: Rhegium.

ρηγμα.def: from ῥήγνυμι (G4486); something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall). KJV: ruin.

ρηγνυμι.def: both prolonged forms of ῥήκω (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of ἄγνυμι (see in κατάγνυμι (G2608))) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; κατάγνυμι (G2608) being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and θραύω (G2352) a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like λύω (G3089)) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions. KJV: break (forth), burst, rend, tear.

ρημα.def: from ῥέω (G4483); an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever. KJV: + evil, + nothing, saying, word.

ρησα.def: probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for H7509); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite. KJV: Rhesa.

ρητωρ.def: from ῥέω (G4483); a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate. KJV: orator.

ρητωσ.def: adverb from a derivative of ῥέω (G4483); out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly. KJV: expressly.

ριζα.def: apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively). KJV: root.

ριζοω.def: from ῥίζα (G4491); to root (figuratively, become stable). KJV: root.

ριπη.def: from ῥίπτω (G4496); a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant). KJV: twinkling.

ριπιζω.def: from a derivative of ῥίπτω (G4496) (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves). KJV: toss.

ριπτεω.def: from a derivative of ῥίπτω (G4496); to toss up. KJV: cast off.

ριπτω.def: a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω (G4474), through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from βάλλω (G906), which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from τείνω (see in ἐκτείνω (G1614)), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse. KJV: cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.

ροβοαμ.def: of Hebrew origin (H7346); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite. KJV: Roboam.

ροδη.def: probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl. KJV: Rhoda.

ροδοσ.def: probably from ῥόδον (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean. KJV: Rhodes.

ροιζηδον.def: adverb from a derivative of ῥοῖζος (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash. KJV: with a great noise.

ρομφαια.def: probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively). KJV: sword.

ρουβην.def: of Hebrew origin (H7205); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite. KJV: Reuben.

ρουθ.def: of Hebrew origin (H7327); Ruth, a Moabitess. KJV: Ruth.

ρουφοσ.def: of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian. KJV: Rufus.

ρυμη.def: prolongation from ῥύομαι (G4506) in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded). KJV: lane, street.

ρυομαι.def: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to ῥέω (G4482) (through the idea of a current; compare ῥύσις (G4511)); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue. KJV: deliver(-er).

ρυπαροσ.def: from ῥύπος (G4509); dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked. KJV: vile.

ρυποσ.def: of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity. KJV: filth.

ρυποω.def: from ῥύπος (G4509); to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally). KJV: be filthy.

ρυσισ.def: from ῥύομαι (G4506) in the sense of its congener ῥέω (G4482); a flux (of blood). KJV: issue.

ρυτισ.def: from ῥύομαι (G4506); a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face). KJV: wrinkle.

ρωμαικοσ.def: from Ῥωμαῖος (G4514); Romaic, i.e. Latin. KJV: Latin.

ρωμαιοσ.def: from Ῥώμη (G4516); Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun). KJV: Roman, of Rome.

ρωμαιστι.def: adverb from a presumed derivative of Ῥώμη (G4516); Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language. KJV: Latin.

ρωμη.def: from the base of ῥώννυμι (G4517); strength; Roma, the capital of Italy. KJV: Rome.

ρωννυμι.def: prolongation from ῥώομαι (to dart; probably akin to ῥύομαι (G4506)); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye). KJV: farewell.
